content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias in second half.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes with 3–5 day moving average filter.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
